channel.title: California Uzbek — Latest
channel.description: Independent analysis · Central Asia & world geopolitics

item.title: Uzbekistan proposes a "one-stop center" for labor migrants heading to Russia
item.description: Citizens could complete medical exams, biometrics and Russian-language testing in one place before departure; the center has not yet been approved.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan requires a certificate for religious preachers as Central Asia tightens religious regulation
item.description: People who publicly preach religion online must now obtain a special certificate; clothing and other religious-life restrictions are also expanding across neighboring states.

item.title: How fasting in Ramadan works: rules, exemptions and fidya
item.description: Fasting in Ramadan (sawm) is one of the Five Pillars of Islam and is obligatory for able, adult Muslims. It runs from true dawn (subh) to sunset (maghrib). Below, the rules of the fast, who is exempt, and the make-up fast (qada), compensation (fidya) and expiation (kaffara) are explained using broadly accepted sources, primarily the Hanafi school. Where the legal schools differ, this is noted.

item.title: Uzbekistan to transfer 11 football clubs, including Pakhtakor, to private trust management
item.description: Entrepreneurs taking a club must cover at least 20% of its annual expenses and receive tax breaks; the state plans to stop financing professional football by 2030.

item.title: At the CAMCA forum in Baku, Uzbekistan proposes a stronger regional body for Central Asia
item.description: Senate First Deputy Chairman Sodiq Safoev called for transforming the heads-of-state Consultative Meeting into an institutional structure.

item.title: 14 servicemen die in Caspian drill: Kazakhstan dismisses its defense minister and detains five officers
item.description: After the September 24 tragedy, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev replaced the defense minister; the Navy chief of staff and other officers are under investigation for negligence.

item.title: The U.S. Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN): how to get one and what it is for
item.description: An ITIN (Individual Taxpayer Identification Number) is a 9-digit number issued by the U.S. Internal Revenue Service (IRS) for people who have a federal tax reporting requirement but are not eligible for a Social Security Number (SSN). It serves one purpose only — federal tax reporting: it does not authorize work, does not change immigration status, and is not a substitute for an SSN. A practical guide based only on verified official sources.

item.title: Uzbekistan joins the CIS: the Alma-Ata Protocol (1991)
item.description: On 21 December 1991, in Alma-Ata (Almaty), Kazakhstan, 11 former Soviet republics signed the Alma-Ata Protocol and Declaration, formally establishing the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS). The documents declared that the USSR 'ceases to exist as a subject of international law and geopolitical reality.' For Uzbekistan, the protocol was signed by President Islam Karimov. It was the first multilateral framework after independence. Based only on verified facts.

item.title: Israel's October 27 election: Netanyahu and Eisenkot neck and neck
item.description: Israel votes for the 120-seat Knesset. Polls show a near-tie between Likud and the Yashar party; the election unfolds against a fragile Gaza ceasefire.

item.title: Getting a U.S. driver's license (DMV): how it works
item.description: In the U.S. a driver's license is issued not by the federal government but by each state's motor-vehicle agency (DMV), so the rules differ from state to state. The common steps are: documents, a written (knowledge) test, a learner's permit, and a road test. From 7 May 2025 the REAL ID requirement is in force — a federally compliant license or a passport is needed to board a domestic flight or enter certain federal buildings. Based on official sources.

item.title: Uzbekistan's president rewards Chess Olympiad winners: $200,000, a house and a car each
item.description: Each member of the gold-winning open team received $200,000, a Volkswagen Teramont Pro and a house; the bronze-winning para-chess team received $50,000, a car and housing each.

item.title: The Uzbek diaspora in China (East Turkestan): how it formed
item.description: The Uzbeks of China are a small but ancient community that has lived for centuries in Xinjiang (East Turkestan). Most descend from merchants who came along the Silk Road from Bukhara, Kokand, Andijan and Samarkand. The community began settling in Xinjiang's cities from the 16th century and grew further after the 18th century. Today they are one of China's 56 officially recognized ethnic groups: the 2020 census counted 12,742. Based only on verified facts.

item.title: Uzbekistan to host the 2027 U-20 World Cup: Mirziyoyev meets Infantino
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and FIFA President Gianni Infantino discussed the Uzbekistan–Azerbaijan U-20 World Cup and opening a regional FIFA office in Tashkent.

item.title: Why Russia's fuel export ban matters for Uzbekistan
item.description: Ukrainian strikes cut Russian petroleum output by more than 30%; Russia banned gasoline and diesel exports through January 31, 2027. Uzbekistan sources about half of its imported petrol from Russia.

item.title: Renting a home or apartment in the USA: the basics for immigrants
item.description: Renting an apartment in the U.S. usually follows the same steps: an application and application fee, a credit and background check, a lease, and a security deposit. Before moving in you often pay the first month's rent, the deposit, and sometimes the last month's rent at once. Discrimination is banned by the 1968 Fair Housing Act. The detailed rules vary from state to state. Based on official and reliable sources.

item.title: Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and the UAE to study the CASA rail route to the Indian Ocean
item.description: The three sides signed a memorandum to study the feasibility of a railway through Afghanistan to Pakistan's seaports.

item.title: Iran's IRGC says it strikes ships daily in the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: IRGC spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi said Iranian forces regularly strike small vessels in the Strait of Hormuz; meanwhile a Qatar-mediated proposal to reopen the strait is under discussion with the US.

item.title: How the Central Bank of Uzbekistan and monetary policy work
item.description: The central bank is the state's bank of issue: it issues the national currency (the som), regulates banks, and runs monetary policy. Founded in 1991; a new law of 11 November 2019 strengthened its independence and set price stability as its primary objective. In January 2020 it adopted an inflation-targeting regime with a medium-term target of 5%. Its main tool is the policy rate: held at 14% since March 2025 (unchanged again at the 16 September 2026 meeting). The som was floated on 5 September 2017. Based on official Central Bank data.

item.title: The Uzbek diaspora in Germany and Europe: how it formed
item.description: The Uzbek community in Europe — especially in Germany — is younger and smaller than those in Russia and the US, but it is growing. Mid-20th century: Turkestani political émigrés; after independence: students and professionals; from 2015: asylum seekers. A key turning point: on 15 September 2024 Germany and Uzbekistan signed a migration and mobility partnership in Samarkand. In 2024 Germany issued the most EU Blue Cards — 56,252. Facts only, sourced.

item.title: Tokayev in Berlin: Ukraine, Russia, and Germany's growing economic interest in Kazakhstan
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met Chancellor Friedrich Merz in Berlin on 29 September, discussing the war in Ukraine, energy, critical minerals and investment; cumulative German investment in Kazakhstan exceeds $8 billion.

item.title: The creation of Uzbekistan's Armed Forces (1992)
item.description: After independence, one of the key tasks of state-building was a national army. On 14 January 1992 Uzbekistan took the units of the former Soviet Turkestan Military District on its territory under national jurisdiction and established the Armed Forces. The Ministry of Defence was founded on 2 July 1992; the first defence minister was Rustam Akhmedov (who led it until 1997). On 29 December 1993 parliament designated 14 January as Defender of the Motherland Day. Verified facts and dates only.

item.title: UN: Terror groups in Afghanistan remain a threat to Central Asia
item.description: According to UN Security Council monitoring reports, Islamic State Khorasan Province is developing a network of cells capable of projecting a threat across the region and internationally; its propaganda is produced in Uzbek and Tajik.

item.title: Consular services and passports for Uzbekistanis abroad
item.description: For Uzbekistan citizens living or staying abroad, embassies and consular sections are the main point of contact: they issue and renew passports, process documents, register civil-status acts (births, marriages), and provide emergency help. Most services first require being on the consular register. The biometric passport dates from 2011, the red international biometric passport from 1 January 2019; from 2021 the ID card is used domestically. The exit-permission sticker was abolished on 1 January 2019. Based on official sources.

item.title: AIIB and Uzbekistan sign a $5 billion infrastructure programme
item.description: An updated multi-year programme signed on the sidelines of the 11th AIIB Annual Meeting in Doha provides for up to $5 billion in financing for infrastructure projects in 2026–2029; the bank also committed a $1.5 million grant to help modernise the power transmission network.

item.title: Cotton-field defoliant sprayed near a school poisons 22 pupils in Uzbekistan's Guzar
item.description: In Guzar district of Kashkadarya, 22 pupils were hospitalized after a defoliant was sprayed on a cotton field beside their school; a criminal case was opened over violations of chemical-handling rules.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Constitutional Court strikes down 10-day border detention without a judge
item.description: The court found provisions of Article 288 of the Code of Administrative Responsibility incompatible with Article 27 of the Constitution; no one may now be held longer than 48 hours without a court decision.

item.title: The U.S. Social Security Number (SSN): how to get it and what it is for
item.description: What the Social Security Number (SSN) is and why it matters (work, wages, taxes, benefits, banking, credit); who can get one and how immigrants obtain it (through the immigrant-visa process or Form SS-5, usually in person); the three card types (unrestricted; “VALID FOR WORK ONLY WITH DHS AUTHORIZATION”; “NOT VALID FOR EMPLOYMENT”); the documents needed; SSN vs. ITIN; the fact that it is free; and protection from fraud. Based on the U.S. Social Security Administration (SSA) and the IRS, as of 2026.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Declaration of State Sovereignty (20 June 1990)
item.description: On 20 June 1990 the Supreme Soviet of the Uzbek SSR adopted the Declaration of State Sovereignty — not independence itself, but a decisive step toward it. The declaration proclaimed the primacy of republican law. This piece sets out its content, the context of the Soviet “parade of sovereignties” (1988–1990), the election of Islam Karimov as the first president on 24 March 1990, the 1989 language law, and the road to full independence on 31 August 1991.

item.title: Putin caps cash rubles taken out of Russia; Uzbekistan is on the list
item.description: Under the new decree, an individual may not take more than 1 million rubles (about $12,300) in cash from Russia to Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Azerbaijan and EAEU states; for legal entities, exporting cash rubles is banned regardless of amount.

item.title: The U.S. retirement system: Social Security, 401(k) and IRA basics
item.description: The U.S. retirement system rests on three pillars: public social insurance (Social Security), employer plans (401(k)), and personal savings (IRA). How you qualify for Social Security (40 credits ≈ 10 years; in 2026, 1 credit = $1,890, up to 4 credits a year); full retirement age (67 for those born after 1960), early (62) and delayed (up to 70) claiming; the FICA tax (6.2% + 6.2%); rules for immigrants and totalization agreements; and the 2026 limits for 401(k) and IRA. Based on the U.S. Social Security Administration (SSA) and the IRS.
